status: explicit coupled fixed-point and critical-trajectory test; coefficients are illustrative truncation data, not a derived Spin(2,3) beta function

interpretation.warning: f and c are not derived for the corpus Spin(2,3) action

gaussianGaugeFixedPoint.classification: both directions relevant in the asymptotic-safety convention theta=-eig(B); finite-scale gauge amplitude remains a free trajectory parameter
gaussianGaugeFixedPoint.fZeroLimit: g is marginally asymptotically free and Lambda_color is an integration constant

interactingBenchmark.classification: gravity is relevant and color is irrelevant, so color has no independent UV integration constant

criticalTrajectory.decision: Within the declared beta system, fixed-point irrelevance plus the gravity crossover removes the independent g3(v) boundary datum.

signAndExistenceTests.cZeroFPositive: only the Gaussian color fixed point exists and theta_g=f>0, leaving the gauge trajectory free
signAndExistenceTests.cZeroFNegative: an interacting root gStar^2=-f/b exists but theta_g=-2f>0, so it is relevant and still free
signAndExistenceTests.requiredForPrediction: an interacting fixed point with negative gauge critical exponent plus a fixed relevant gravity trajectory and matching map

issues: perturbative gravitational correction to the gauge kinetic term has appeared gauge dependent or absent in different calculations
functional-RG fixed-point coordinates depend on gauge, regulator and truncation
higher-dimensional operators can move or remove the interacting root represented by c
Einstein-Cartan or broken Spin(2,3) theory need not share the metric-gravity universality class
physical predictivity requires stable critical exponents and an observable matching map, not fixed-point coordinates alone
schemeAndTruncationBoundary.decision: The toy removes g3(v) only by supplying f, c, the gravity trajectory and matching. Those are not yet corpus-derived universal data.

closureConditions: nonperturbative definition of the quantum broken-Spin(2,3) plus portal theory
gauge-gravity fixed point with finite-dimensional UV critical surface
irrelevant color exponent stable under systematic truncation enlargement
unique critical trajectory through all selector thresholds and induced operators
gauge-invariant observable matching to low-energy MSbar color and pure-YM threshold
programmeDecision: Asymptotic safety can remove the color boundary in a specified beta system, but presently trades g3(v) for unestablished fixed-point, critical-trajectory and universality-class data.
